findings.title: New safe host entry can reach undefined float-to-int frame conversion
findings.evidence: lightning_update_impl assigns t*10 or t*frames directly to int. The newly public safe Rust methods accept any f32 input, and the Lua reader accepts arbitrary finite exact-f32 values. A cloud with start_time=f32(1e30),length1 followed by current_time0 survives the single-day wrap and yields t about -1e30; casting the resulting frame to int is outside the representable range and undefined C behavior. Nonfinite intermediate products can similarly reach the cast. Existing tests cover ordinary, midnight, subnormal and unknown-type cases but do not make these new safe entry paths defined.
findings.requested_change: Before each int conversion, reject nonfinite or out-of-int-range products under the existing FP guard, clear/refuse with a named error and commit no queue change. Preserve the original defined expression order and numerical result; do not clamp, add arbitrary input preconditions or introduce a float narrowing merely to check. Add finite safe-API/atomic-refusal controls for these unsafe casts and retain all existing seeds/matrices/oracles.

findings.title: Frame handshake and update replies can expose invalid model/renderer accesses
evidence: NeedFrames is accepted for any first update and immediately calls frames_of without checking the mirror contains a live forked dependency. A replacement provider can request frames with an empty or cloud-only queue. The Core helper then dereferences texture_animations[lightning_strike_animation] without availability/index checks; texture_animations is initialized NULL in3dobjid.c86 and its count initially0. The documented uninitialized headless model dependency becomes a crash before a named refusal.

Completed update validation checks integer shape, finite float fields and retained strike attributes, but allows any current_frame_number for a live forked strike. A provider can return frame-1 orINT_MAX, pass validation and commit the mirror. The genuine compiled draw_3d_lightning_strike indexes texture_indices[current_frame_number] directly at3dstrike.c514; this is an out-of-bounds consumer, not hypothetical headless dormancy.
findings.requested_change: Validate NeedFrames against an existing live forked mirror dependency before model lookup. Make the remaining animation-frame lookup check actual texture-table/index/count availability and refuse safely under a provider/model marker; do not reproduce host expiry math in Core. Validate live forked reply frame indices against a usable model-frame domain before mirror commit, including a provider bypassing NeedFrames, while preserving atomic refusal and defined original outcomes. Add finite direct malformed-provider/lookup controls using the actual C consumer; no generic DLL/model framework or D5 deferral.

findings.title: New refusal witness labels a stop without verifying engine_failure and absent result rows
findings.evidence: In withheld/malformed modes, ran=false unconditionally makes result_row=false and the delegate output is never read. requests>0 plus substring occurrence of the expected marker anywhere in the caught error is enough to emit stopped_at_boundary. Thus the promised engine_failure/no-result facts are asserted rather than checked. A delegate/output error after a result, whose diagnostic/path contains the marker, can be misclassified as the intended engine stop; existing scripted tests exercise only the expected clean stop.
findings.requested_change: Check the actual delegate record even when pcall fails: require its case2 engine_failure at the matching boundary and no result row. Reject delegate/output/witness failures as such, preserving ordinary outer mlua traceback. Add bounded contradictory-result/own-output-error controls. Reuse the existing finite delegate protocol; no new trace or physics framework.
